reason: Recurring class of work (refilling an idle agent queue from PRDs/design) had no skill; the episode shows a reusable order, citation style, product-decision handling, and the encolar-includes-merge preference that a future session would otherwise rediscover only from memory files.

User asked how the overnight factory run went. The night was idle because the queue was empty until 09:20, and the diagnosis path (cola vacía in the out log, lock error in the err log) is not in this skill. Adding it as a subsection keeps the idle-agents trigger the one place to look.

A night's researcher and planner runs were cut by per-run caps (0.61 USD over 0.60; 26 turns over 25). The skill had no guidance on budget_exceeded, so the refill stalled and the failed entries kept showing as fallidas.

A cut planner run had already created epic #1032 and stories #1033-#1045; re-queuing its original "create the epic" task would have duplicated them. The refill must check existing artifacts and phrase retries as completion.
The queue runs entries in file order with no dependency check, so queuing a base story together with its dependents would start the dependents from a main that lacks the base.
gh pr checks --watch output was swallowed and grep returned empty lines; statusCheckRollup gave the real conclusions. The merge step needs a reliable CI read.
A refill queued models already present in data/raw on main, wasting a researcher run. Issue and PR lists alone did not catch it.

The episode was a user asking "podemos meter mas tareas en la cola?" and the agent rebuilt the refill procedure from scratch; the skill never fired because its trigger only named an empty queue or idle agents. Broadening the trigger to the words the user actually types routes this class of request here.

The user asked whether more tasks could go in the queue. The agent counted gaps (25 models without images, 169 retrieved in November, 45 in October), chose to queue only the missing photos in batches of 5–6 under the researcher's remaining budget, and deliberately held back the refresh because the project rule is discover-and-complete before refresh. That sequence is reusable and was not written down.

Appending as text is the rule, but the episode's append was only validated by the test suite. A direct parse of the file right after the append catches a broken YAML entry before the PR is opened, and the comment header per batch made the appended block readable in the diff.
